section_summary: A secret 1944 report assesses Japan’s oil transport fleet, including tanker losses, construction and the use of cargo ships and barges. A separate 1941 memorandum compares petroleum exports to Japan with 1940 figures and lists outstanding licenses and applications for Japan and occupied China.

subfiles.title: Japan’s Oil Transport Fleet
subfiles.about: Assessment of Japan’s wartime capacity to transport oil by tanker and substitute vessels.
subfiles.summary: The report estimates tanker losses and new construction, describes oil carriage by cargo ships and barges, and concludes that continued losses will strain Japan’s transport capacity.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Petroleum Exports and Export Licenses for Japan
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, Chief, Division of Controls
subfiles.about: Petroleum shipments to Japan and pending export licenses for Japan and occupied China.
subfiles.summary: Compares first-half 1941 petroleum exports to Japan with 1940, then lists licensed but unshipped quantities and applications being held.
